name: Project Initiation Request
one_liner: The one-page ask: here is the problem, roughly this big, please let us write a Business Case.
purpose: The Project Initiation Request is a project's starting point and formalises its initiation: it captures the current situation (problem, need or opportunity) and the desired outcomes so they can be explored further. It carries high-level effort, cost, timeframe and type of delivery, the expected impact and success criteria, the link to the organisation's strategic direction, and the first assumptions, constraints and risks. Approving it authorises work on a more elaborate Business Case — not the project.
approved_by: Project Owner (PO), or a higher-level Appropriate Governance Body (AGB) for a formal approval route
inputs: A problem, a need or an opportunity expressed by the initiator
Lessons learned from similar past projects

lifecycle.what: Drafted, submitted, approved; content copied into Business Case and Charter
Lifecycle already ended — superseded, not maintained
Archived as the project's origin document

fields.what: Initial project title proposal — provisional, will be confirmed in the Business Case and Charter.
fields.castor: Project CASTOR — Renewal of the Lending Operations System (LOS)

fields.what: Any person, usually from the business community, can define a project request; the person raising it is named here.
fields.who: Anyone · in practice the PO delegates to the BM
fields.castor: Grace Hopper, Senior Loan Operations Officer, for Lending Operations

fields.what: The organisation or unit requesting the project — the side that will own and benefit from the outputs.
fields.castor: European Stability Mechanism — Lending Operations Division, Luxembourg (Kirchberg)

fields.what: The organisation funding and mainly benefiting from the project's outputs nominates a person as owner of the project.
fields.castor: Florence Nightingale, Head of Lending Operations Division

fields.what: The date the Project Initiation Request is completed — the project's formal starting point.
The organisation that will execute the project and be accountable for the deliverables nominates a person to act as supplier.
fields.castor: Leonardo da Vinci, Head of IT & Digital Division

fields.what: The appropriate decision maker as specified in the organisation's governance structure — informal (PO) or formal (AGB).
fields.castor: Corporate Investment Board (CIB), chaired by Lorenzo de' Medici, Deputy Managing Director

fields.what: High-level estimate in person-days; any other known costs should be mentioned here too.
The date the project delivery is needed by the business — a need, not yet a commitment.
Tick one: In-house, Outsourced, Mix, or Not-known — the first signal about procurement and the Outsourcing Plan.
fields.castor: Mix — in-house core team plus outsourced platform implementation

fields.what: Why a project should be initiated: the situation to be addressed as a need, a problem, an opportunity, or a combination.
fields.castor: LOS is 14 years old; disbursement instructions re-keyed by hand across three systems; reconciliation takes three working days.

fields.what: The legal basis, if any, plus the link to the organisation's strategic goals; can be a directive from senior management.
fields.castor: No dedicated legal act; ESM lending mandate, plus two open Internal Audit findings on segregation of duties and audit-trail completeness.

fields.what: Main expected outcomes — the future or desired state after the change; measurable benefits must be linkable to them.
fields.castor: Straight-through processing from loan agreement to disbursement and repayment; instrument-agnostic product configuration; same-day reconciliation.

fields.what: Impact of the situation and/or solution internally (processes, people, culture) and on external stakeholders; kept high level.
fields.castor: 40 loan administrators change how they work; Finance & Control, Risk and Legal processes touched; no impact on beneficiary member states.

fields.what: High-level criteria on which the proposed project can be judged a success or failure; may cover scope, schedule and costs.
fields.castor: SC1 disbursement cycle 5 working days → 1; SC3 new instrument onboarding 9 months → 6 weeks; SC5 open audit findings 2 → 0.

fields.what: Assumptions on business, technology, resources, environment, scope, expectations or schedule — treated as facts, still to be validated.
fields.castor: A configurable market platform can cover all ESM instruments by configuration; business experts released part-time from Lending Operations.

fields.what: Key constraints on schedule, budget, resources or products to be used or acquired, including compliance and external constraints.
fields.who: BM drafts · SP and PO confirm
fields.castor: €8.4 m envelope and 26 months; no change freeze breaches during bond rollovers; procurement lead time before contract award.

fields.what: Initial risks identified at this stage, focused on the business risks rather than technical detail.
fields.who: BM drafts · PO owns business risk
fields.castor: Common-backstop ratification incomplete (Italy has not ratified), so backstop scope may shift; scarce LOS knowledge concentrated in few people.

traps: Anyone may initiate it, but the BM is Responsible and the PO Accountable (A/S).
The PSC is n.a. here — it does not exist yet, so it cannot approve the request.
Approving the request authorises the Business Case, not the project.
Its lifecycle ends once the Business Case and Charter exist; those two stay live.
The PM is normally not yet assigned — the SP appoints the PM after the Business Case.

LOS dates from the EFSF era and is 14 years old. Disbursement instructions are re-keyed by hand between LOS, treasury and the payment gateway; reconciliation takes three working days.
Disbursement cycle 5 working days → 1; reconciliation 3 days → same day; new instrument onboarding 9 months → 6 weeks; 2 open audit findings → 0.
